title: happens-before
summary: Answers whether one event (a write, a read, a call, a source line, an Application.Run) has happened before another on every execution: YES, NO or MAY
intro: Ask it when the order of two things matters and you want a proof, not a guess: is the connection opened before every query, is the flag written before it is read, is Randomize called before Random, is FormatSettings set before the first format call, does A happen before Application.Run. It proves order inside a routine, across calls, and across initialization sections, the program block and handlers (program-order). It reads the index, names every site of both events and answers YES or NO only when it can prove it; everything else is MAY, with the reason per site. Exit 0 = YES, 1 = NO or MAY, 2 = error.

help: drag-lint happens-before     (--a <event> --b <event> | --preset <name>) --db <db> [--json] [--max-routines N] [--max-seconds S]
has event A happened before event B, on every execution? (read-only, on demand)
<event>: write:<QName> | read:<QName> (unit variable, class var, instance field), call:<QName> (the call sites
the index resolves to that routine), extcall:<Name>[,<Name>...] (calls of routines the index does not hold, by name),
extwrite:<Name>[,<Name>...] (assignments to or through a variable the index does not hold), app-run:<program>|*
(the top-level Application.Run of that program block, * = every program), site:<file>:<line>[:<col>].
YES = every site of B runs after A (proven). NO = a B runs with no A before it (proven: A has no site, or
every site of A runs after a site of B). MAY = not proven either way; every doubt answers MAY and each
judged site carries a reason: a-not-on-every-path, a-in-other-routine, a-site-uncertain, a-sites-incomplete,
b-sites-incomplete, no-b-site, no-routine-body, budget (NO: a-never-happens, b-first).
Proofs: same-routine, callee (a certain call of a routine that always performs A), callers (A before every
call of B's routine), check-init (write:T before read:T through the check-init solver), program-order
(initialization chain, program block, handler order, call chains: A first from every root that reaches B;
also proves the b-first NO).
Pre-check: a site of B that no routine performing A can reach in the call graph answers MAY a-in-other-routine
at once (limit pre-check, no routine body solved); when it refutes every B site the b-first proof is skipped.
--preset randomize = --a extcall:Randomize --b extcall:Random.
--preset format-settings = --a extwrite:FormatSettings --b extcall: of the RTL format / parse routines.
--preset before-app-run --a <event> = B is app-run:* (does A happen before Application.Run?).
In-force question (lane HB6): --a free:<QName> / final-free:<QName> / held:<QName> is a STATE that lasts
from a site of A until a re-assignment (free) or any other mention of the lock (held); B is often use:<QName>.
free / final-free: YES = a site of B runs with A in force, NO = none can (b-never-after-a) or A never happens,
MAY = b-may-run-after-a. held: YES = in force at every site of B. Proofs in-force, reassigned-first,
finalization-order. JSON carries question: in-force.
--preset use-after-free --a <QName> = A free:X, B use:X (wanted: NO).
--preset finalization --a <QName> = A final-free:X, B use:X (wanted: NO; unit variable or class var).
--preset lock-held-when --a <QName> --b <event> = A held:L (wanted: YES).
Limits of the in-force question: aliases-not-followed, callbacks-not-modelled.
Limits: sites are not instances (instance-insensitive); extcall: matches by name (matched-by-name);
pre-check (call graph alone, no body solved); program-order: relied-on-handler-order and
program-order: relied-on-indirect-edges (what a program-order YES leaned on; a NO never does).
--max-routines N = routine bodies to solve (default 2000); --max-seconds S = wall-clock cap (default 60, 0 = none).
json: verb, preset?, a / b {event, kind, name, complete, incomplete[], sites[{file, line, col, routine, definite, note}]},
verdict, proven, summary, reasons[], methods[], judged[{side, file, line, col, routine, proven, method, reason, why}],
limits[], budget{routines, ms, exhausted}.
Exit 0 = YES, 1 = NO or MAY, 2 = usage / unknown target / missing or stale --db, 3 = unknown flag.

questions.ask: Is Open always called before Exec?
Is this flag written before it is read, on every execution?
Does this line always run before that line?
Is Randomize called before every Random?
Are the FormatSettings assigned before every format or parse call?
Does this write happen before Application.Run?
Is this object used after it was freed?
Is this global used after its unit finalization freed it?
Is this lock held whenever that field is written?
